stem: Which taxpayer qualifies for head of household status for 2025?

choices.text: A single taxpayer who lives alone and has no dependents
A widow whose spouse died in 2025
A married taxpayer living with her spouse all year
choices.explanation: Married taxpayers living together can't use HOH.

choices.text: An unmarried parent maintaining a home for her son
choices.explanation: Correct. HOH: unmarried, maintains a home for a qualifying person for more than half the year.

explanation: HOH: unmarried, maintains a home for a qualifying person for more than half the year.

stem: For 2025 the qualifying-relative gross income limit is $5,200. Which person can be a qualifying relative (not a qualifying child) for 2025?

choices.text: The taxpayer's 15-year-old daughter who lived with him all year
A friend who lived with the taxpayer for only 6 months
choices.explanation: Household members must live there all year.

choices.text: His widowed father with $4,000 of interest, whom he supports
choices.explanation: Correct. Qualifying relative: relationship, gross income under $5,200, over half support.

choices.text: The taxpayer's brother, who earned $12,000 of wages

explanation: Qualifying relative: relationship, gross income under $5,200, over half support.

stem: The 2025 standard deduction for married filing jointly is $31,500, and the additional amount is $1,600 for each spouse age 65 or older. A couple filing jointly for 2025 includes one spouse age 67 and one age 60; neither is blind. What is their standard deduction (excluding the separate senior deduction)?

choices.explanation: This adds the additional amount for both spouses; only one is 65 or older.
This omits the additional amount for the 67-year-old spouse.
This uses half of the additional amount.
Correct. 31,500 + 1,600 for the one spouse age 65 or older = 33,100.

explanation: The additional standard deduction applies per spouse who is 65 or older (or blind).
reviewNote: Uses a One Big Beautiful Bill Act (P.L. 119-21) amount for 2025. Verify against current IRS guidance and exam materials.

stem: Which item is taxable to the recipient?

choices.text: $50,000 of life insurance proceeds paid on the insured's death
A $5,000 cash award for winning an essay contest
choices.explanation: Correct. Prizes and awards are generally included.

choices.text: Compensatory damages for a physical injury

explanation: Prizes and awards are generally included.

stem: An employee receives employer-paid group-term life insurance coverage of $50,000 and a $300 holiday gift card. What is included in gross income?

choices.text: The cost of the coverage only
choices.explanation: The coverage is excluded; the card isn't.

choices.text: The cost of $50,000 of coverage plus $300
choices.explanation: The first $50,000 of coverage is excluded.
Correct. §79 excludes $50,000 of coverage; cash equivalents are never de minimis.

explanation: §79 excludes $50,000 of coverage; cash equivalents are never de minimis.

stem: A cash-basis taxpayer is insolvent by $15,000 when a lender cancels $40,000 of debt (not in bankruptcy). What is included in income?

choices.explanation: Correct. Excluded to the extent of insolvency: 40,000 − 15,000 = 25,000 included.

explanation: Excluded to the extent of insolvency: 40,000 − 15,000 = 25,000 included.

stem: A taxpayer receives $6,000 of unemployment compensation and $8,000 of child support. How much is included in gross income?

choices.explanation: Includes child support and excludes unemployment — reversed.
Correct. Unemployment compensation is taxable; child support isn't.

explanation: Unemployment compensation is taxable; child support isn't.

stem: A taxpayer rents a vacation home for 120 days and uses it personally for 20 days. How is it classified?

choices.text: A rental property with full deductions allowed
choices.explanation: Personal use exceeds 14 days (greater of 14 or 10% of 120 = 14).

choices.text: A home rented for fewer than 15 days
A residence; deductions limited to rental income
choices.explanation: Correct. Personal use of 20 days exceeds the greater of 14 days or 12 days (10% of 120).

explanation: Personal use of 20 days exceeds the greater of 14 days or 12 days (10% of 120).

stem: A sole proprietor incurs $400 for business meals with clients and $900 for golf outings with clients. What is deductible?

choices.explanation: Entertainment isn't deductible and meals are 50%.

explanation: Meals 50% (200); entertainment 0.

stem: Which is a deduction for AGI in 2025?

choices.text: Home mortgage interest on a residence
Contributions to a health savings account
choices.explanation: Correct. HSA contributions made by the individual are above-the-line.

choices.text: Gambling losses up to gambling winnings

explanation: HSA contributions made by the individual are above-the-line.

stem: For 2025 the deduction phases out for a single active participant between MAGI $79,000 and $89,000. A single taxpayer (MAGI $70,000) is covered by a 401(k) and contributes $7,000 to a traditional IRA in 2025. How much is deductible?

choices.explanation: Correct. MAGI is below the $79,000 phase-out start.
MAGI is below the phase-out range.
That was an older contribution limit.

explanation: Active participants phase out at $79,000–$89,000 (single) for 2025.

stem: In 2025, an itemizing taxpayer with AGI of $60,000 gives $40,000 cash to a public charity. What is the 2025 deduction?

choices.explanation: Correct. Cash to public charities: 60% × 60,000 = 36,000; 5-year carryforward.

explanation: Cash to public charities: 60% × 60,000 = 36,000; 5-year carryforward.

stem: Which is deductible as an itemized deduction for 2025?

choices.text: Real estate taxes on a principal residence
choices.explanation: Correct. Real property taxes are deductible subject to the SALT limit.

choices.text: Tax preparation fees for a personal return
Foreign real property taxes on a vacation home
Interest on personal credit card balances

explanation: Real property taxes are deductible subject to the SALT limit.

stem: A single taxpayer has QBI of $100,000 from a non-service business and taxable income before QBI of $90,000 (no capital gains). The taxpayer is below the threshold. What is the QBI deduction?

choices.explanation: Adds the components instead of taking the lesser.

stem: The 2025 child tax credit is $2,200 per qualifying child under 17 ($500 for other dependents); the phase-out begins at MAGI $400,000 for joint filers. A married couple filing jointly (MAGI $180,000) has three children aged 5, 11, and 16. What is their 2025 child tax credit?
explanation: 2025 CTC is $2,200 per qualifying child under 17; the joint phase-out starts at $400,000.
reviewNote: Uses a One Big Beautiful Bill Act (P.L. 119-21) amount for 2025. Verify against current IRS guidance and exam materials.

stem: A student's parents (MAGI $150,000, joint) pay $3,000 of qualified tuition for her first year of college. What is the American opportunity credit?
explanation: AOTC = 100% of the first $2,000 + 25% of the next $1,000.

stem: Which credit can produce a refund even if the taxpayer owes no tax?
explanation: The EIC is refundable.

stem: A self-employed individual has $100,000 of net SE income and no wages. What is the deduction for half of SE tax (rounded)?

choices.explanation: Uses only the Social Security rate.

stem: A C corporation owns 85% of a domestic subsidiary and receives $200,000 of dividends. What is the dividends-received deduction?
explanation: 80% or more ownership → 100% DRD.

stem: A corporation's 2025 taxable income before the charitable contribution deduction and the DRD is $500,000. It has no NOL or capital loss carryovers. It contributed $70,000 cash to charity. What is the charitable deduction?
explanation: The limit is 10% of taxable income figured without the charitable deduction, the DRD, and any NOL or capital loss carryback (an NOL carryforward would reduce the base; IRC §170(b)(2)(D)). 10% × 500,000 = **50,000**; the other 20,000 carries forward 5 years.

stem: Which item is added to book income in reconciling to taxable income?

choices.text: Excess of tax depreciation over book depreciation

choices.explanation: Correct. Federal income tax isn't deductible, so it's added back.

explanation: Federal income tax isn't deductible, so it's added back.

stem: A corporation has 2025 taxable income of $200,000 before a $300,000 NOL carryforward from 2020. What is 2025 taxable income?

choices.explanation: The NOL can't create a loss.

explanation: Post-2017 NOL deduction limited to 80% of TI.

stem: When is the final estimated tax installment due for a calendar-year corporation?

choices.explanation: Correct. Corporate installments: 15th day of the 4th, 6th, 9th, and 12th months.

explanation: Corporate installments: 15th day of the 4th, 6th, 9th, and 12th months.

stem: A 50% partner's share of ordinary income is $40,000 and of tax-exempt interest $2,000; she receives $25,000 cash. Beginning basis is $10,000. What is her ending basis?
explanation: Income items increase basis; distributions decrease it.

stem: Which partnership item is **not** separately stated?

choices.explanation: Correct. It nets into ordinary business income.

explanation: Ordinary operating expenses net into ordinary business income.

stem: A partnership pays a partner a $20,000 guaranteed payment for services. How does the partner treat it?

choices.text: As a tax-free distribution of cash
As ordinary income subject to SE tax
choices.explanation: Correct. Guaranteed payments are ordinary income and SE income.

choices.text: As a reduction of basis only

explanation: Guaranteed payments are ordinary income and SE income.

stem: Which requirement must be met to elect S corporation status?

choices.explanation: Correct. S corporations may have only one class of stock (voting differences allowed).

explanation: S corporations may have only one class of stock (voting differences allowed).

stem: An S corporation shareholder has stock basis of $5,000 and no debt basis. Her share of the corporation's loss is $12,000. How much is deductible?

choices.explanation: Correct. Losses limited to stock + debt basis; 7,000 is suspended.

explanation: Losses limited to stock + debt basis; 7,000 is suspended.

stem: A former C corporation (S since 2022) has accumulated E&P. Which distribution source comes first?

choices.explanation: Correct. Ordering: AAA → E&P → basis → gain.

explanation: Ordering: AAA → E&P → basis → gain.

stem: Which item is added to book income on Schedule M-1?

choices.text: Tax depreciation in excess of book depreciation
Life insurance proceeds received on a key officer
Charitable contributions in excess of the 10% limit
choices.explanation: Correct. Excess charitable contributions are book expenses not deducted.

choices.text: Interest received on municipal bonds held

explanation: Excess charitable contributions are book expenses not deducted.

stem: Book income is $300,000, including $66,000 of federal income tax expense and a $10,000 net capital loss. What is taxable income before special deductions (no other differences)?

A corporation's Schedule M-2 shows beginning retained earnings of $400,000, net income per books of $120,000, and cash distributions of $50,000. It also recorded a $10,000 prior-period adjustment increasing retained earnings. What is ending retained earnings?
A single taxpayer has 2025 modified AGI of $260,000, including $30,000 of net investment income. What is her net investment income tax?

choices.explanation: Correct. 3.8% × the lesser of NII (30,000) or MAGI over $200,000 (60,000).
That applies 3.8% to the 60,000 excess of MAGI over the threshold.
That applies 3.8% to all of MAGI.
0.9% is the additional Medicare tax rate, not the NIIT rate.

explanation: NIIT = 3.8% × the lesser of net investment income or MAGI above $200,000 (single): 3.8% × $30,000 = $1,140.

stem: A taxpayer's 2024 AGI was $180,000 and his 2024 tax was $30,000. His 2025 tax is expected to be $40,000. What is the minimum he must pay through withholding and timely estimates to avoid an underpayment penalty?

choices.explanation: 100% of prior-year tax is enough only if prior-year AGI was $150,000 or less.
90% of current-year tax works but isn't the minimum here.
Correct. Prior-year AGI over $150,000 requires 110% of prior-year tax (33,000), which is less than 90% of current-year tax (36,000).
Paying 100% of current-year tax isn't required.

explanation: Safe harbor: the lesser of 90% of current-year tax or 100% of prior-year tax (110% when prior-year AGI exceeded $150,000). Lesser of $36,000 and $33,000 = $33,000.

stem: Cove Partners reports: revenue $500,000; operating expenses $300,000; guaranteed payments to a partner $60,000; net §1231 gain $20,000; charitable contributions $5,000. What is Cove's ordinary business income?

choices.explanation: That nets the separately stated §1231 gain and charity into ordinary income.
Correct. 500,000 − 300,000 − 60,000 = 140,000; the §1231 gain and charity are separately stated.
Guaranteed payments are deductible in computing ordinary income.
Charitable contributions are separately stated, not deducted.

explanation: Guaranteed payments are deducted in computing ordinary business income; §1231 gains and charitable contributions are separately stated.

stem: An S corporation shareholder's stock basis at January 1, 2025 is $20,000. Her 2025 share of items: ordinary business income $30,000; tax-exempt interest $2,000; cash distribution $10,000. What is her stock basis at December 31, 2025?
explanation: Stock basis increases for all income items, including tax-exempt income, and decreases for distributions: $20,000 + $32,000 − $10,000 = $42,000.

stem: A C corporation with taxable income before special deductions of $400,000 receives $100,000 of dividends from a domestic corporation in which it owns 30%. What is its dividends-received deduction?

choices.explanation: Correct. 20%-to-under-80% ownership gives a 65% DRD; the taxable income limit (65% × 400,000) doesn't bind.
The limit is 65% of taxable income, but the deduction can't exceed 65% of the dividends.

explanation: 30% ownership → 65% DRD: 65% × $100,000 = $65,000, below the 65% × taxable income limit.

stem: A C corporation has 2025 taxable income of $500,000 before any NOL deduction and a $600,000 NOL carryforward from 2022. What NOL deduction is allowed for 2025?

choices.explanation: Correct. Post-2017 NOLs offset only 80% of taxable income: 80% × 500,000.
Post-2017 NOLs can't reduce taxable income to zero.
The deduction can't exceed the 80% limit.
That is 80% of the NOL, not of taxable income.

explanation: NOLs arising after 2017 are carried forward indefinitely and limited to 80% of taxable income: $400,000; $200,000 carries forward.

stem: Trent Co. has $2,000,000 of apportionable business income. Its State Z factors are sales 40%, property 25% and payroll 25%; State Z uses an equally weighted three-factor formula. Trent also earns $100,000 of nonbusiness interest, allocated to its commercial domicile in another state. What is Trent's State Z taxable income?

choices.explanation: The nonbusiness interest is allocated to the domicile state, not apportioned.
Correct. (40% + 25% + 25%) ÷ 3 = 30%; 30% × 2,000,000 = 600,000. The interest is allocated elsewhere.
That uses the sales factor alone.
The interest belongs to the domicile state, not State Z.

explanation: Apportionment percentage 30% × $2,000,000 = $600,000; nonbusiness interest is allocated to the commercial domicile.

stem: A seller of tangible goods ships to customers in State W from its out-of-state plant. Which additional activity in State W would give State W income tax nexus despite P.L. 86-272?

choices.text: Sending sales representatives who only solicit orders approved out of state
choices.explanation: That is exactly the activity P.L. 86-272 protects.

choices.text: Advertising its products on State W radio stations and websites
choices.explanation: Advertising is part of protected solicitation.

choices.text: Shipping all orders by common carrier from outside State W
choices.explanation: Shipping from outside the state is part of the protected pattern.

choices.text: Keeping a stock of inventory in a State W warehouse to fill orders
choices.explanation: Correct. Property such as in-state inventory goes beyond solicitation and creates nexus.

explanation: P.L. 86-272 protects only solicitation of orders for tangible goods approved and filled from outside the state. In-state inventory is property that creates nexus.

stem: Dana's spouse died in 2024. Dana hasn't remarried and maintains a home for her dependent son all of 2025. What is Dana's best filing status for 2025?

choices.explanation: Correct. It is available for the two years after the year of death with a dependent child.

choices.text: Married filing jointly with the estate
choices.explanation: Joint filing was available only for 2024, the year of death.
Qualifying surviving spouse gives better rates.
She qualifies for a more favorable status.

explanation: A qualifying surviving spouse may use joint rates for the two years after the spouse's death if she maintains a home for a dependent child.

stem: For the qualifying child test, a child must be:

choices.text: Under 17 at the end of the year
choices.explanation: Under 17 is the child tax credit age test.

choices.text: Under 19, or under 24 if a student
choices.explanation: Correct. The age limit doesn't apply if the child is permanently and totally disabled.

choices.text: Any age, if living with the taxpayer

explanation: IRC §152(c)(3): a qualifying child must be under 19, under 24 if a full-time student, or any age if permanently and totally disabled.

stem: What is the maximum portion of Social Security benefits included in gross income?

choices.explanation: Correct. Up to 85% of benefits may be taxable, depending on provisional income.
Benefits can be taxable above the base amounts.

explanation: IRC §86: depending on provisional income, 0%, up to 50%, or up to 85% of benefits are included in gross income.

stem: Which employer-provided benefit is excluded from an employee's gross income?

choices.text: Cash bonuses for meeting sales goals
A gift card for $100 at year-end
choices.explanation: Cash equivalents are never de minimis.
Correct. De minimis fringe benefits are excluded.

explanation: IRC §132(e): de minimis fringes, such as occasional snacks or coffee, are excluded; cash and cash equivalents are taxable.

stem: Which amount received in 2025 is included in gross income?

choices.explanation: Correct. Unemployment benefits are fully taxable.
Child support isn't income to the recipient.
Gifts are excluded from the donee's income.

choices.text: Proceeds of a life insurance policy paid at death

explanation: IRC §85 includes unemployment compensation; gifts, child support and life insurance death proceeds are excluded.

stem: A taxpayer rents her vacation home for 12 days in 2025 and uses it personally for 40 days. How is the rental income treated?

choices.text: Included, with expenses deductible in full
Excluded from income; no rental deductions
choices.explanation: Correct. Rentals of fewer than 15 days are ignored.

choices.text: Included, with expenses limited to income
choices.explanation: That applies to longer rentals with significant personal use.

explanation: IRC §280A(g): if a dwelling is rented for fewer than 15 days, the rent is excluded and no rental expenses are deductible.

stem: What is the maximum student loan interest deduction for an eligible taxpayer?

choices.explanation: The limit is per return, not per student.
Correct. Up to $2,500 is deductible for AGI.

explanation: IRC §221: student loan interest of up to $2,500 is deductible for AGI, phased out at higher modified AGI.

stem: A taxpayer with AGI of $80,000 itemizes and paid $9,000 of unreimbursed medical expenses in 2025. What medical deduction is allowed?

choices.explanation: Only the excess over 7.5% of AGI is deductible.
The floor is 6,000; the deduction is the excess.

explanation: IRC §213: medical expenses are deductible to the extent they exceed 7.5% of AGI.

stem: A student in her second year of college has $3,000 of qualified tuition in 2025, and her parents qualify for the American opportunity credit. What is the credit?

choices.explanation: Correct. 100% of the first 2,000 + 25% of the next 1,000.
That is the lifetime learning credit (20% × 3,000).

explanation: AOTC: 100% of the first $2,000 and 25% of the next $2,000 of qualified expenses, per student, for the first four years; 40% refundable.

stem: A sole proprietor has 2025 net self-employment income of $50,000 and no wages. What is the self-employment tax?

choices.explanation: That applies only the 12.4% Social Security rate.

explanation: SE tax = net earnings × 92.35% × 15.3% (below the wage base); half is deductible for AGI.

stem: A C corporation has 2025 taxable income of $300,000. What is its regular income tax?
explanation: IRC §11(b): C corporations pay a flat 21% on taxable income.

stem: For 2025, a corporation has taxable income of $500,000 before the charitable deduction and DRD, and gave $70,000 to charity. What is its charitable deduction?

choices.explanation: Correct. Limited to 10% of taxable income before charity and the DRD.
The excess carries forward five years.

explanation: IRC §170(b)(2): 2025 corporate charitable deductions are limited to 10% of taxable income computed before the charitable deduction, DRD, NOL carryback and capital loss carryback.

stem: A new corporation incurs $12,000 of organizational costs and begins business on October 1, 2025. What is its 2025 deduction for these costs?

choices.explanation: The remainder is also amortized from October.

explanation: IRC §248: deduct up to $5,000 (reduced over $50,000) and amortize the rest over 180 months from the month business begins.

stem: A corporation's book income is $400,000, after $84,000 of federal income tax expense and including $10,000 of municipal bond interest. There are no other differences. What is taxable income?

choices.explanation: Federal tax expense is added back.
Municipal interest must also be removed.

explanation: Schedule M-1: add back federal income tax expense and subtract tax-exempt interest.

stem: A large corporation (taxable income of $1 million or more in a prior three-year year) wants to avoid an estimated tax penalty. Which safe harbor may it use for all four installments?

choices.explanation: Correct. A large corporation may use the prior-year safe harbor only for the first installment.
Large corporations can't use the prior-year rule after the first installment.

explanation: IRC §6655(d): large corporations must base installments on the current year's tax, except the first installment may use the prior year.

stem: A partner contributes land (basis $30,000; fair value $50,000) subject to a $10,000 mortgage that the partnership assumes. She receives a 25% interest. What is her outside basis?

choices.explanation: Liability relief and her share of the debt must be reflected.
Basis carries over; it isn't fair value.
Her 25% share of the mortgage adds back 2,500.

explanation: IRC §722 and §752: carryover basis, decreased by liabilities assumed by the partnership and increased by her share of partnership liabilities.

stem: Guaranteed payments to a partner for services are:

choices.explanation: They are deductible payments for services.

choices.text: Deductible; ordinary income to the partner
choices.explanation: Correct. They are also self-employment income to the partner.

choices.text: Taxed as long-term capital gain to the partner

explanation: IRC §707(c): guaranteed payments are deductible in computing ordinary income and are ordinary (and self-employment) income to the partner.

stem: Which corporation is eligible to elect S status?

choices.text: A corporation with a C corporation shareholder
A corporation with a nonresident alien shareholder
A corporation with voting and nonvoting preferred stock
choices.explanation: Differences in voting rights are fine, but preferred stock creates a second class.

choices.text: One with 90 individual owners and one stock class
choices.explanation: Correct. It meets the 100-shareholder and single-class tests.

explanation: IRC §1361(b): a domestic corporation with no more than 100 eligible shareholders (individuals, estates, certain trusts and exempt organizations) and one class of stock.

stem: An S shareholder has stock basis of $5,000 and loans to the corporation with a basis of $8,000. Her share of the 2025 ordinary loss is $20,000. How much loss may she deduct?

choices.explanation: Correct. Losses are limited to stock plus debt basis; the excess carries forward.

explanation: IRC §1366(d): an S shareholder deducts losses up to stock basis plus debt basis; the excess carries forward.

stem: A state double-weights the sales factor. A corporation's factors there are sales 50%, property 30% and payroll 20%, and its business income is $800,000. What business income is apportioned to the state?

choices.explanation: That uses an equally weighted three-factor formula.
That uses the sales factor alone.
Only the apportioned share is taxed.

explanation: Double-weighted sales: (2 × sales + property + payroll) ÷ 4.

stem: Which requirement must an unmarried taxpayer meet to file as head of household?

choices.text: Have AGI below a set income limit
choices.explanation: There is no income limit for head of household.

choices.text: Itemize deductions on Schedule A for the year
choices.explanation: Filing status doesn't depend on itemizing.

choices.text: Pay over half the cost of a qualifying home
choices.explanation: Correct. The taxpayer must maintain the home for a qualifying person (a parent may live elsewhere).

explanation: IRC §2(b): an unmarried taxpayer who pays more than half the cost of keeping up a home that is the principal home of a qualifying person for over half the year may file as head of household.

stem: Which receipt is included in gross income?

choices.text: The federal income tax refund itself

choices.explanation: Post-2018 alimony isn't income to the recipient.

choices.text: Interest on a federal tax refund
choices.explanation: Correct. Interest on a tax refund is taxable interest income.

explanation: Interest on refunds is taxable; federal refunds, post-2018 alimony and workers' compensation are excluded.

stem: A lender cancels $30,000 of a taxpayer's credit card debt. Immediately before, the taxpayer's liabilities were $100,000 and assets $80,000. How much is included in gross income?

choices.explanation: Correct. The exclusion is limited to insolvency of 20,000.
Insolvency excludes part of the canceled debt.
Only the insolvent amount is excluded.

explanation: IRC §108(a)(1)(B): canceled debt is excluded to the extent the taxpayer is insolvent (liabilities exceed assets by $20,000).

stem: A self-employed taxpayer uses 400 square feet of her home exclusively and regularly as her principal place of business. Using the simplified method, what is the maximum home office deduction?

choices.explanation: Only 300 square feet count under the simplified method.
Correct. $5 per square foot, up to 300 square feet.
The rate is $5 per square foot, capped at 300.
The cap is 300 square feet, not 240.

explanation: Rev. Proc. 2013-13 simplified method: $5 per square foot of home office space, up to 300 square feet ($1,500).

stem: A sole proprietor spends $4,000 on business meals with clients and $3,000 on tickets to sporting events for clients in 2025. What is deductible?

choices.explanation: Correct. Meals are 50% deductible; entertainment isn't deductible.

explanation: IRC §274: business meals are generally 50% deductible; entertainment expenses are not deductible.

stem: Which item is deductible for AGI by a self-employed individual?

choices.text: The full amount of her self-employment tax
choices.explanation: Only half of SE tax is deductible.

choices.text: Charitable gifts made by her business

choices.explanation: Correct. Self-employed health insurance is an adjustment to income.

explanation: IRC §162(l): self-employed health insurance premiums are deductible for AGI (limited to net SE earnings); half of SE tax is also an adjustment.

stem: For 2025, the itemized deduction for state and local taxes is limited to $40,000 for taxpayers with MAGI of $500,000 or less. A married couple with MAGI of $300,000 pays $25,000 of state income tax and $20,000 of real property tax. What is their SALT deduction?

choices.explanation: The cap applies to the total.
Both income and property taxes count.

explanation: IRC §164(b)(6) as amended by P.L. 119-21: for 2025, state and local taxes are deductible up to $40,000 ($20,000 MFS), reduced above $500,000 of MAGI.
reviewNote: Uses the 2025 SALT cap of $40,000 set by P.L. 119-21; confirm against current IRS guidance.

stem: An itemizer with AGI of $80,000 donates long-term stock (fair value $30,000; basis $10,000) to a public charity in 2025. What is the deduction for 2025?

choices.explanation: Correct. Capital gain property at fair value is limited to 30% of AGI.
Appreciated long-term stock is deducted at fair value.
The 60% limit is for cash gifts.

explanation: IRC §170(b)(1)(C): gifts of capital gain property to public charities are deducted at fair value, limited to 30% of AGI (24,000), with a five-year carryforward.

stem: A single parent with AGI of $70,000 pays $4,000 of day care in 2025 for one child so she can work. What is her child and dependent care credit?

choices.explanation: Expenses are capped at $3,000 for one child.
The 35% rate applies only at low AGI.
Correct. Expenses are limited to 3,000, times 20% at this AGI.
That uses the $6,000 cap for two or more.

explanation: IRC §21 (2025): 20% of up to $3,000 of expenses for one qualifying person once AGI exceeds $43,000.

stem: A single employee earns $260,000 of wages in 2025. What additional Medicare tax applies?
explanation: IRC §3101(b)(2): 0.9% of wages above $200,000 (single).

stem: A corporation receives $100,000 of dividends from a 25%-owned domestic corporation. Its taxable income before the DRD is $80,000, including the dividends. What is its DRD?

choices.explanation: Correct. The deduction is limited to 65% × 80,000 because the full 65,000 wouldn't create an NOL.
The deduction is a percentage of income.

explanation: IRC §246(b): the 65% DRD is limited to 65% of taxable income before the DRD unless the full DRD creates or increases an NOL.

stem: A C corporation has a $30,000 capital loss and a $10,000 capital gain in 2025. How is the net loss treated?

choices.explanation: Corporations can't deduct net capital losses against ordinary income.
Corporate capital losses carry back 3 and forward 5.
Correct. Corporations deduct capital losses only against capital gains.

explanation: IRC §1211(a), §1212(a): corporate capital losses offset capital gains only; the excess carries back three years and forward five as short-term.

stem: What is the original due date of a calendar-year C corporation's 2025 Form 1120, and how long is the automatic extension?

choices.explanation: Correct. Form 1120 is due on the 15th day of the 4th month, with a six-month extension.
March 15 is the Form 1065 and 1120-S due date.

explanation: IRC §6072: calendar-year C corporation returns are due April 15; Form 7004 extends six months, to October 15.

stem: An accrual-basis corporation accrues a $20,000 bonus to its cash-basis majority shareholder-employee at December 31, 2025 and pays it on February 1, 2026. When may it deduct the bonus?

choices.text: In 2025, because it was accrued by year-end
In 2026, when the shareholder is paid
choices.explanation: Correct. §267(a)(2) defers the deduction until the related cash-basis payee includes it.
The 2½-month rule doesn't apply to related parties.

choices.text: Never, because it is a dividend

explanation: IRC §267(a)(2): an accrual-basis payer deducts amounts owed to a related cash-basis payee only when the payee includes them in income.

stem: When is a calendar-year partnership's 2025 Form 1065 due, without extension?

choices.explanation: April 15 is the due date for individuals and C corporations.
January 31 is for Forms W-2 and 1099-NEC.
Correct. The 15th day of the third month after year-end.
May 15 is the Form 990 due date.

explanation: IRC §6072(b): partnership returns are due on the 15th day of the third month after year-end.

stem: A partner's outside basis at January 1, 2025 is $20,000. Her 2025 share of items: ordinary income $15,000; tax-exempt interest $1,000. She receives a $8,000 cash distribution. What is her basis at year-end?

choices.explanation: Both increases count, then distributions reduce basis.

explanation: IRC §705: basis increases for the partner's share of all income, including tax-exempt income, and decreases for distributions.

stem: An S corporation with no accumulated E&P distributes $15,000 cash to a shareholder whose stock basis is $12,000. How is the distribution taxed?

choices.explanation: Correct. Distributions reduce basis; the excess is treated as gain from the sale of stock.
With no E&P there is no dividend.

explanation: IRC §1368(b): distributions from an S corporation without E&P are tax-free to the extent of basis; the excess is gain from the sale of stock.

stem: For an S election to be effective for a calendar-year corporation's 2025 tax year, it generally must be filed by:

choices.explanation: A late election applies to the next year unless relief applies.
Correct. The election is due by the 15th day of the third month of the tax year.
The deadline is the 15th day of the third month.

explanation: IRC §1362(b): an election made by the 15th day of the third month of the tax year is effective for that year.

stem: Which organization may engage in substantial lobbying related to its exempt purpose without losing its exemption?

choices.explanation: Substantial lobbying can cost a charity its exemption.
Correct. Social welfare organizations may lobby extensively for their purposes.
Churches are §501(c)(3) organizations with the same limit.

explanation: §501(c)(3) organizations may not devote a substantial part of activities to lobbying; §501(c)(4) organizations may lobby as a primary activity.

stem: After South Dakota v. Wayfair (2018), a state may require a remote seller to collect sales tax based on:

choices.text: Only physical presence, such as an office or employees

choices.explanation: P.L. 86-272 concerns income taxes on tangible goods.

choices.text: Economic nexus, such as sales above a threshold
choices.explanation: Correct. Physical presence is no longer required for sales tax nexus.

explanation: Wayfair allowed states to impose sales-tax collection duties on remote sellers with economic nexus, commonly $100,000 of in-state sales.
